UPSTREAM: mwifiex: fix use-after-free for FW reinit errors If we fail to reinit the FW when resetting the device (in the synchronous version of mwifiex_init_hw_fw() -> mwifiex_fw_dpc()), mwifiex_fw_dpc() will tear down the interface and free up the adapter. But we don't actually check for all failure cases of mwifiex_fw_dpc(), so some of them fall through and dereference adapter->fw_done with a freed adapter, causing a use-after-free bug. In any case, mwifiex_fw_dpc() will always signal FW completion -- in the error OR success case -- so at best, this was repeat work. Let's not do it. Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master commit ce8fad9a1f09009ec3918a99685d9e3176f50ce3) BUG=b:36006967 TEST=kevin wifi; and `echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000\:01\:00.0/reset` Change-Id: Idd154307d33d3e395685b1a3c4691dce237d5675 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/474993 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: mwifiex: catch mwifiex_fw_dpc() errors properly in reset When resetting the device, we take a synchronous firmware-loading code path, which borrows a lot from the asynchronous path used at probe time. We don't catch errors correctly though, which means that in the PCIe driver, we may try to dereference the 'adapter' struct after mwifiex_fw_dpc() has freed it. See this (erronous) print in mwifiex_pcie_reset_notify(): mwifiex_dbg(adapter, INFO, "%s, successful\n", __func__); Let's instead refactor the synchronous (or "!req_fw_nowait") path so that we propagate errors and handle them properly. This fixes a use-after-free issue in the PCIe driver, as well as a misleading debug message ("successful"). It looks like the SDIO driver doesn't have these problems, since it doesn't do anything after mwifiex_reinit_sw(). Fixes: 4c5dae59d2e9 ("mwifiex: add PCIe function level reset support") Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master commit 755b37c93a069ff0882411630a06e90b3193d092) BUG=b:36006967 TEST=kevin wifi; and `echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000\:01\:00.0/reset` Change-Id: Ib19f4320c796e5f6481be6d56b5789dc4b299fec Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/474994 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

lakitu: systemd: do not disable blkid When systemd is configured with --disable-blkid systemd-udevd will use blkid installed by util-linux. That version does not understand --noraid and --offset flags, hence we get the errors listed below. systemd-udevd[400]: IMPORT{builtin}: 'blkid --offset=$env{ID_CDROM_MEDIA_SESSION_LAST_OFFSET}' unknown /lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:60 systemd-udevd[400]: IMPORT{builtin}: 'blkid --noraid' unknown /lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:63 systemd-udevd[400]: IMPORT{builtin}: 'blkid' unknown /lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:66 BUG=b:32978263 TEST=image boots without above errors Change-Id: Ia500fb016fb3a11a8ea767edda93070d49423698 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/476077 Commit-Ready: Andrey Ulanov <andreyu@google.com> Tested-by: Andrey Ulanov <andreyu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Daniel Wang <wonderfly@google.com>
